extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students learning algebraic number theory (Frobenius elements, Chebotarev, Artin reciprocity)
extracted.subtask_description: Lecture-note style exposition on Frobenius elements, their relation to splitting of primes, control of polynomial factorization, and the statement/implications of Artin reciprocity (ray class groups, conductors, Takagi existence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and characterization of Frobenius element
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L/K be a Galois extension and p an unramified prime of K with P above it in L. There is a unique element Frob_P ∈ Gal(L/K) obeying Frob_P(α) ≡ α^{N(p)} (mod P) for all α ∈ O_L (Theorem 63.5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the defining criterion for the Frobenius element; the residue-field map induced by Frob_P is the 'power-of-N(p)' map. Example computations (e.g. in cyclotomic or quadratic extensions) illustrate how to identify Frob_P concretely. The existence requires p unramified in L/K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic Frobenius equals σ_p; splitting criterion in cyclotomic fields
rubrics_metrics.description: In L = Q(ζ_q) with ζ_q a primitive qth root of unity, for a rational unramified prime p and P above it we have Frob_P = σ_p (Lemma 62.4.1). Consequently a rational prime p splits completely in O_L if and only if p ≡ 1 (mod q) (Question 62.4.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the action σ_n : ζ ↦ ζ^n to identify Frobenius; this gives the classical congruence criterion for complete splitting in cyclotomic fields. This is the prototypical example showing how congruence conditions on p control splitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction property of Frobenius elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If L/Q and K/Q are Galois, P is a prime of L above a prime p of K (unramified), then Frob_P restricted to K equals Frob_p: Frob_P|_K = Frob_p (Theorem 62.5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows Frobenius elements 'behave well with restriction' and allows one to compare Frobenius upstairs and downstairs; used in proofs such as quadratic reciprocity to relate splitting in intermediate fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Frobenius equals inertial degree; identity iff full splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: ord Frob_P = f(P | p), the inertial degree of P over p. In particular, Frob_P = id if and only if p splits completely in L/K (Lemma 63.5.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus cycle lengths of Frobenius correspond to residue-field extension degrees; this links group-theoretic properties of Frobenius to arithmetic decomposition data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius elements control prime decomposition via cycle structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Q ⊆ E ⊆ K with K/Q Galois and H the subgroup corresponding to E. For an unramified rational prime p and P above it, the factorization pattern of p in E (inertial degrees partition of n = [E:Q]) equals the cycle structure of Frob_P acting on the left cosets G/H (Theorem 62.7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the action of Frob_P as a permutation on cosets; its cycle decomposition gives the partition of n by inertial degrees. This is the generalization of the quadratic-splitting argument and is the core principle to deduce splitting behaviour from Galois action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of three viewpoints on factorization / polynomial factorization
rubrics_metrics.description: For α an algebraic integer with minimal polynomial f and splitting field K, and p unramified in K, the following coincide: (i) factorization pattern of p in E = Q(α); (ii) factorization pattern of f (mod p); (iii) cycle structure of Frob_P acting on the roots of f (Theorem 62.7.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a practical tool: to understand f (mod p) one can compute the Frobenius cycle structure (or vice versa). The bijection between roots and cosets G/H (H stabilizer of α) underlies the equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Chebotarev to realize prescribed Frobenius conjugacy classes (existence of primes)
rubrics_metrics.description: By Chebotarev density (used implicitly), for any conjugacy class (or element in abelian case) in Gal(K/Q) there exist infinitely many unramified rational primes q whose Frobenius at a chosen P is that class (illustrated in §62.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently one can construct primes giving desired cycle structures (used to force irreducibility or particular factorization patterns). The argument in the IMO 2003 example uses Cauchy's theorem + Chebotarev to find primes q with given Frobenius of prime order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of modulus (including infinite primes) and congruence modulo infinite primes
rubrics_metrics.description: A modulus m is a formal product over finite and infinite primes, with ν(p)=0 for complex infinite primes and ν(p)≤1 for real infinite primes. For a real infinite prime σ, a ≡ b (mod p) means σ(a/b) > 0; for finite primes it is the usual a − b ∈ p^{ν(p)} (Section 63.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends classical 'mod m' arithmetic to number fields by including signs at real embeddings; it is necessary to define ray classes and the Artin conductor correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and finiteness of ray class group CK(m)
rubrics_metrics.description: IK(m) is fractional ideals of K relatively prime to m; PK(m) is subgroup generated by principal ideals (α) with α ≡ 1 (mod m). The ray class group CK(m) = IK(m)/PK(m) is finite (Definition 63.3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CK(m) generalizes the ideal class group and will serve as the target for Artin reciprocity. Examples for K = Q show how finite and infinite parts affect CK(m) (Examples 63.3.3–63.3.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Congruence subgroups and Takagi existence theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: A congruence subgroup H satisfies PK(m) ⊆ H ⊆ IK(m). For fixed modulus m, every congruence subgroup H equals H(L/K,m) for a unique abelian extension L/K (Takagi existence theorem, Theorem 63.6.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the bijection between (suitable) subgroups of IK(m) and abelian extensions of K, i.e., class field theory in the ray-class formulation. Use this to enumerate abelian extensions via subgroups of CK(m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin map and conductor; Artin reciprocity's dependence on residue classes mod conductor
rubrics_metrics.description: For an abelian extension L/K and modulus m divisible by all ramified primes, the Artin map (L/K •) : IK(m) ↠ Gal(L/K) is defined and surjective with kernel H(L/K,m). There exists a conductor f = f(L/K) such that PK(m) ⊆ H(L/K,m) ⊆ IK(m) iff f | m. Consequently, for primes p ∉ Ram(L/K), the Artin symbol (L/K p) depends only on the class of p modulo f (Theorem 63.6.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conductor f is the minimal modulus capturing ramification; when m is multiple of f the Artin map factors through the ray class group CK(f) and yields an explicit reciprocity law: Frobenius/Artin symbol is determined by residue class modulo f. Examples: quadratic fields and cyclotomic fields show how classical reciprocity laws arise as special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin symbol in abelian extensions generalizes classical residue symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: If L/K is abelian and p unramified, the Frobenius element Frob_P is independent of the choice of P and is denoted the Artin symbol (L/K p). This generalizes the Legendre (quadratic) and higher residue symbols (Examples 63.5.7, 63.5.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpreting classical quadratic/cubic residue characters as Artin symbols situates reciprocity laws in the Artin-reciprocity framework and explains why those symbols depend only on p modulo some conductor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of infinite primes in extensions (ramification of ∞)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infinite primes correspond to embeddings K → C. A real infinite prime σ of K lifts to m infinite primes τ of L; if any τ above σ is complex then σ ramifies in L/K. An infinite prime of K is always unramified in L/K when K is totally complex (Section 63.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determines which infinite primes must be included in the modulus/conductor and affects the ray class group and Artin map; check signatures (r,s) to decide ramification at infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion-reversing correspondence between fields and congruence subgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix modulus m divisible by conductors. For abelian extensions L/K and M/K, L ⊆ M if and only if H(M/K,m) ⊆ H(L/K,m) (Lemma 63.6.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encapsulates the Galois/ideal-theoretic duality: larger fields correspond to smaller kernels under the Artin map. The proof uses functoriality of Frobenius under restriction and Takagi existence theorem for the converse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic extension realizes lower bound: kernel equals PQ(m∞)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Q(ζ_m)/Q one has H(Q(ζ)/Q, m∞) = PQ(m∞), so the Artin map IQ(m) → Gal(Q(ζ)/Q) is given by p ↦ (x ↦ x^p) and the conductor divides m∞ (Example 63.6.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit identification shows cyclotomic fields achieve the minimal congruence subgroup and recovers classical statements: Frobenius is literally 'p (mod m)' in Gal(Q(ζ)/Q). Use this as a model for computing conductors and Artin maps.
